title: HelioHealth POC scoping - open model shortlist
summary: POC scoping for HelioHealth clinical-note summarization and multilingual triage: discussed success criteria (quality thresholds, latency, cost), workload sizing, benchmark plan, timeline, and shortlist of open models. Security/HIPAA and VPC deployment options are top priorities. Next steps: Redwood to run initial benchmark on 1k de-identified prompts, send model matrix and pricing, schedule dedicated benchmark window.
next_steps: Redwood: send model performance matrix + recommended quantization profiles (Maya) - due 2025-11-24
HelioHealth: share 1,000 de-identified clinical prompts and sample transcripts (Sarah) - due 2025-11-25
Schedule 2-hour dedicated benchmark window w/ GPU reserved (Liam+Raj) - target week of 2025-12-01
Redwood: provide SOC2/HIPAA and architecture note for VPC deployment (Maya/Tom) - due 2025-11-26
action_items: Maya: prepare model shortlist + latency/cost estimates and send matrix - 2025-11-24
Liam: prepare benchmark plan + template for logs and KPIs - 2025-11-23
Sarah: anonymize and drop 1k prompt/testcases into shared S3 bucket - 2025-11-25
Tom: confirm HelioHealth legal/infosec checklist items and provide lead contact - 2025-11-27
transcript: 00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining on time, uh we're going to kick off, this is Maya from Redwood Inference, with Liam our SE. 00:06 Sarah Lopez: hi Maya, hi Liam, thanks, we got the calendar, excited to scope a poc. 00:12 Raj Patel: yep, CTO Raj here, quick heads up security will be on the call briefly. 00:17 Maya Chen: great, quick agenda - success criteria, workload, benchmarks, model shortlist, timeline; sound good? 00:25 Nina Gomez: yep, that's good. 00:27 Liam O'Connor: cool, I'll jump into some performance notes as we talk models, but first, Sarah, can you outline the primary use cases and what success looks like for HelioHealth? 00:38 Sarah Lopez: sure. So topline - clinical note summarization for physicians and a multilingual triage assistant for intake. For summarize - quality is critical, we need high factuality and low hallucination. Our acceptance criteria is ROUGE-ish metrics are okay but we will rely on clinician evals, target 90% pass rate on a 5-point rubric. For triage, latency under 500ms median for single-turn, and support for Spanish and Portuguese with decent accuracy. 01:08 Maya Chen: got it - so two verticals: summarization (factuality, hallucination risk) and multilingual triage (latency + language coverage). For the POC are you expecting production load or a sample of traffic? 01:20 Sarah Lopez: sample, but representative - about 2k requests per day with bursty peaks up to maybe 40 concurrent at peak hours; avg request length ~1-2 paragraphs, sequence length ~200-600 tokens. 01:35 Raj Patel: and we will want to test on de-identified EHR notes, also need HIPAA compliance and VPC option for data plane. 01:44 Maya Chen: totally understood. On the HIPAA/VPC point, Redwood Private or Dedicated can be set up, we support VPC peering, KMS and audit logs. We'll attach the infra note later but Tom - anything specific from security? 01:56 Tom Alvarez: yeah we need encryption at rest, KMS integration, audit trail retention for 7 years, and an architecture whitepaper showing how keys and logs are handled. Also interested in pen-testing posture and SOC2 evidence. 02:10 Maya Chen: we'll include SOC2 and HIPAA attestation docs; expectation is Redwood can host in a VPC with customer-managed KMS. 02:18 Nina Gomez: on timelines - we ideally want a 6-week POC; two weeks ingest and sanity tests, two weeks benchmark + eval, two weeks iteration. Is that realistic? 02:29 Liam O'Connor: yes that's feasible. We'll need the test set to run reproducible benchmarks, and a reserved window for the heavy GPU runs. 02:36 Sarah Lopez: about models - we're leaning toward open models for cost and auditability, can you recommend a shortlist? 02:42 Maya Chen: absolutely. For summarization and factuality we typically shortlist a few families: Llama 3 derivatives (if available), Mistral/Orca variants, and some instruction-tuned LLMs like Falcon-180B-instruct or open-repos of Llama-2-70b. For multilingual triage, we consider models that have shown good cross-lingual performance - Mistral mixes and Polyglot/Meta variants. 03:08 Raj Patel: curious about tradeoffs - like performance vs cost and quantization impacts. 03:13 Liam O'Connor: right so tradeoffs - bigger dense models usually have higher quality for abstractive summarization, but you can often get near-similar quality with careful instruction-tuning and 8-bit or 4-bit quantization. For latency we can use smaller distilled variants or enable caching and batching in the runtime. Also note that sequence length and KV cache impacts memory footprint - 600 tokens pushes memory. 03:35 Maya Chen: also worth noting model families differ on hallucination tendencies - some instruction-tuned checkpoints have better groundedness. We'll provide a matrix of expected latency/throughput on our infra for each model and quantization profile. 03:47 Nina Gomez: okay and for multilingual what would you recommend as first-pass models? 03:51 Liam O'Connor: I'd recommend two tracks: a mid-sized multilingual model (e.g., Mistral-X-multilingual or XLM-Falcon variants) for triage for good latency, and a larger model for summarization where factuality matters - maybe a Llama3-70b style or Falcon-180B-instruct if you can tolerate cost. We can also test instruction-tuned smaller models for summarization to see where the quality inflection is. 04:16 Sarah Lopez: how do we measure hallucination in bench? We have clinician reviewers but need an automated proxy. 04:21 Liam O'Connor: automated proxies: factuality scoring using QA-based metrics (answering questions from notes), semantic overlap, entity preservation. We'll pair automated metrics with blinded clinician evals. 04:32 Raj Patel: on benchmarks, we need to capture latencies (p50/p95), token throughput, cost per 1k requests, and failure modes. 04:40 Maya Chen: yes, our template captures p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, cost estimate, and sample outputs. We'll also log model divergence and hallucination flags. 04:50 Sarah Lopez: what's the expected per-request cost for those bigger models? Ballpark. 04:54 Liam O'Connor: ballpark: on hosted inference scaled to our infra, Falcon-180B-instruct in 4-bit quant might be X per 1k tokens, Llama-class 70b in 4-bit slightly cheaper or comparable depending on kernel efficiencies. We'll include concrete dollar estimates in the matrix - depends on batching and prefix caching. 05:10 Raj Patel: we may prefer Redwood Dedicated if the cost at scale is better and we need predictable throughput, but initial POC can be hosted. 05:19 Maya Chen: makes sense. For POC we usually run on hosted for speed, then move to Dedicated or Private for later phases. We can emulate Dedicated throughput during benchmarks. 05:27 Nina Gomez: who will own evaluation and signoff? We need a success document. 05:31 Sarah Lopez: Head of ML (Sarah) with Product signoff (Nina), and technical acceptance by Raj. So thresholds: clinician pass rate 90% for summaries, median latency <500ms for triage; p95 <1.2s; cost per request under internal threshold TBD. 05:49 Maya Chen: good to have clear gates. We'll build a success criteria doc and run it by you. 05:54 Tom Alvarez: quick security note - for the benchmark data we want to ensure it's de-identified and not stored beyond the benchmark window; logs should be exportable. 06:03 Liam O'Connor: yes, we can run ephemeral benchmark instances, ensure logs are exported to your S3, and we will delete any cached prefixes if you request. 06:12 Sarah Lopez: ok great. On model shortlist can you list the initial 4-5 models you plan to test? 06:17 Maya Chen: prelim shortlist - 1) Mistral-Med-multilingual-13B (or closest), 2) Falcon-180B-instruct (4-bit), 3) Llama-2/3-70B-instruct family variant, 4) Vicuna-style 33B distilled for latency test, 5) XLM-Falcon multilingual 40B. We will also include a small open instruction model baseline (e.g., Llama-2-13B-instruct) for reference. Note: some of these names may vary depending on availability. 06:57 Raj Patel: sounds reasonable - we want to see quality curves vs cost curve. 07:01 Maya Chen: yes we'll provide quality vs cost and latency profiles, plus recommended quantization (8-bit/4-bit) and expected throughput. 07:09 Nina Gomez: how long do these benchmarks take? 07:12 Liam O'Connor: for a 1k sample test for full metrics maybe a day of runs if we reserve GPU capacity; end-to-end with clinician evals takes the two-week benchmark window you proposed. 07:23 Sarah Lopez: ok let's pick dates: we'll aim to hand over data by 11/25, Redwood to run benchmarks 12/1-12/3, preliminary results by 12/5, clinician evals 12/6-12/12, final review 12/15. 07:37 Maya Chen: that aligns with the 6-week plan. I'll send calendar invites for the 2-hour reserved run window. 07:43 Raj Patel: a few technical questions: does Redwood support pinned model versions, rollbacks, and can you do canary traffic for the POC? 07:52 Liam O'Connor: yes pinned versions, canary routing, and automatic fallback to smaller variants if latency spikes - we can show the console demo in the next session. 08:00 Tom Alvarez: about KMS integration - what providers do you support? 08:04 Maya Chen: we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, HashiCorp Vault, and HSM integrations; we'll include the architecture note. 08:12 Sarah Lopez: any gotchas with tokenization and medical abbreviations? 08:16 Liam O'Connor: tokenization rarely breaks things but abbreviations can change model behavior; we recommend a small preprocessing normalization or prompt engineering to reduce ambiguous expansions. We'll help craft that template. 08:29 Nina Gomez: will Redwood provide prompt templates and evaluation scripts? 08:32 Maya Chen: yes we'll provide prompt templates, evaluation harness, and sample scoring scripts; open-source friendly. 08:39 Sarah Lopez: competitors - we looked at Anthropic for safety tooling, but open models are attractive for cost and data residency. 08:47 Maya Chen: noted. We'll include a competitive note in the doc. 08:51 Raj Patel: anything else? 08:53 Nina Gomez: just that we'll need to include legal for the POC addendum. 08:56 Maya Chen: we'll loop in our legal and send a POC addendum template. 09:00 Maya Chen: recap of next steps, action items - Maya will send model matrix, Liam benchmark plan, Helio shares data, Tom confirms checklist. Thanks everyone. 09:12 Sarah Lopez: thanks, talk soon. 09:15 Meeting ended.
